newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Judge sets hearing in Manila water project case.
newsitem.headline: Judge sets hearing in Manila water project case.

text.p: A Philippine judge heard arguments on Monday on a petition to halt the privatisation of the Manila Waterworks Sewerage System (MWSS) but made no decision.

Manila regional trial court judge Inocencio Malalian set another hearing for Wednesday on an application by a group of people, representing former and current officials of Rizal province as well as a former military general, to stop the sale.
The group says President Fidel Ramos' authority to privatise MWSS given by the Water Crisis Act lapsed as of December 1995.

The same group had earlier secured a 72-hour temporary restraining order (TRO) against the sale. But the TRO elapsed a day before four groups submitted their technical and financial bids last January 6.
The technical bids are to be cleared by an MWSS committee by Wednesday and the financial bids of those companies which pass the scrutiny will be opened on Thursday.
During Monday's hearing, government lawyers argued that the regional trial court had no jurisdiction to issue an injunction on government projects.
They said two presidential decrees had earlier been issued against such injunctions with regards to the development of the country's natural resources.

Four groups are vying for the two 25-year contracts to supply water to Metro Manila. They are: the consortium of Bechtel Corp of the United States, United Utilities Plc)and Ayala Corp ; Lyonnaise des Eaux SA in collaboration with Benpres Holdings Corp ; Anglian Water Plc along with Australia Water Technologies Pty Ltd and Metro Pacific Corp ; and Compagnie Generale des Eaux EAUG.P with Aboitiz Equity Ventures Inc.
The two winners of the contracts for East and West Manila are expected to invest a total of $7.0 billion over the next 25 years to improve water and sewerage services.
